chunks: Concerning a man who contracts mut'ah marriage, does it render him muhsan? He said: “No; that only applies to the permanent thing.”

As for what the report contains, that “if he commits zina with his wife's slave-woman without her permission, then upon him is the like of what is upon the fornicator: he is to be flogged one hundred,” his statement “he is to be flogged one hundred” does not conflict with the possibility that rajm is also obligatory upon him. For we have already explained that the muhsan must have both matters combined upon him when he is of the description that we mentioned. There is nothing in it indicating that rajm is not obligatory, and what proves that rajm is obligatory upon him is what has already been established: that he is a fornicator, and everything that indicates that the fornicator must undergo rajm indicates its obligatoriness upon him. His statement, peace be upon him, “upon him is the like of what is upon the fornicator,” also confirms that and further clarifies what we have mentioned, as does what he narrated:
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham and Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from one whom he mentioned, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام: concerning...

key_terms.أَتُحْصِنُهُ: does it render him muhsan, legally protected through valid marital status
key_terms.اَلرَّجْمُ: stoning as a prescribed hadd punishment in the relevant case
key_terms.اَلْمُحْصَنَ: the legally muhsan person subject to the ruling discussed
key_terms.يُجْلَدُ مِائَةً: he is to be flogged one hundred lashes

ai.seo_question: Does mut'ah marriage make a man muhsan, and does the punishment of one hundred lashes exclude rajm in zina cases?
ai.summary: This passage discusses a legal ruling concerning zina and the status of ihsan in relation to mut'ah marriage. It states that mut'ah does not establish the state relevant here, and it argues that the mention of one hundred lashes does not negate the additional application of rajm for the muhsan in the specified circumstances.
